findings.problem: The proof rebuilds by hand a standard Mathlib fact: an algebra hom out of an MvPolynomial ring is determined by its values on the variables. It uses `MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext`, a `change` to expose `algebraMap`, `f.commutes` and a `simp` call, then `rw [he]; exact hf`. About ten lines go on re-deriving `f = aeval (f ∘ X)`.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace lines 70–79 with the existing lemma `MvPolynomial.aeval_unique`:
```
  have he : f = MvPolynomial.aeval (fun i => f (MvPolynomial.X i)) :=
    MvPolynomial.aeval_unique f
  -- `aeval x` is `eval₂Hom (algebraMap ℂ Γ(C,A.U)) x`, and this algebraMap is `A.scalar` by `toAlgebra`
  have hs : Function.Surjective (MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => f (MvPolynomial.X i)) := he ▸ hf
  exact hs
```
The final `exact hs` depends on `MvPolynomial.aeval_eq_eval₂Hom` being `rfl`, and on `algebraMap ℂ Γ(C,A.U)` unfolding to `A.scalar` through `RingHom.toAlgebra`. If that defeq check is too slow, `simpa [MvPolynomial.aeval_eq_eval₂Hom] using hs` or a `show` is a fallback.
findings.benefit: The proof now states the idea directly: a surjection from a polynomial ring is the evaluation at the images of the variables. It no longer has the ad hoc `ringHom_ext` split into a constants case and a variables case, or the `change` on algebraMaps. It also uses named Mathlib lemmas, so a reader can look them up instead of re-checking a bespoke argument.

evidence.excerpt: theorem aeval_unique (φ : MvPolynomial σ R →ₐ[R] S₁) : φ = aeval (φ ∘ X)
theorem aeval_eq_eval₂Hom (p : MvPolynomial σ R) : aeval f p = eval₂Hom (algebraMap R S₁) f p :=
FiniteType R S ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] S), Surjective f
